name: security-aws-kms-encryption-context-review
intent: KMS decrypt/data-key authority across encryption contexts and services
artifacts: Key policy/grants, caller IAM context, encryption-context constraints, ciphertext origin and service path.
trace: Resolve effective KMS authority and whether trusted encryption context or ViaService constraints bind the intended tenant/workload. Treat encryption context as authenticated metadata, not secret data.
experiment: Use an owned test key and synthetic ciphertext locally/in an authorized sandbox; compare rightful context and principal with a mismatched tenant context.
disproof: The ability to invoke an SDK or read a key ARN is not decryption authority; cryptographic rejection alone does not test IAM separation.
repair: Constrain principal/service/context authorization and verify legitimate decrypt plus cross-context denial.
branch_decisions: Encryption context is authenticated additional data, not encrypted secret storage. Follow the exact context supplied to KMS and conditions in both key and identity policies, including grants and service-mediated calls. A caller able to choose a tenant context must still be authorized to use that tenant; mere knowledge of the context is not entitlement.
operational_method: Start from key type and exact API: encryption context applies to supported symmetric encryption operations, not every asymmetric or HMAC operation. Record the literal map sent to Encrypt/Decrypt and the condition/grant used. Distinguish EncryptionContextEquals from EncryptionContextSubset constraints and compare the caller-supplied tenant map with the policy-expected map. A local cryptographic context mismatch is not evidence that IAM separates tenants; inspect the grant/policy path independently.
